title: Leaving home after a violent night and being locked out
summary: After four record dates he came home to a drunk, accusing wife, left for the YMCA and found the locks changed.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: So I was sitting in the room one day, and I called Helen --

My wife Helen, yes, and I was really hurting and I really wanted to go back home -- in fact, I left home because of the violence that was going on, I just got tired of it because I don't consider myself a violent person, but I had to be in self defense.
So one morning, I had recorded all day -- I did 4 record dates that day, starting out at ten o'clock that morning, I didn't finish until three the following morning.

And I'm coming home, and as I turned the corner, I saw the light on in the living room and I knew what to expect when I saw the light on. But with all due respect to her, she had a problem with the bottle. And whenever I saw the light on, I knew that she was sitting there drunk, waiting on me. And the first thing she said to me was: 'What woman were you out with?' and I told her, I said, 'Well, look, you've got my schedule there, you know that I been working all day; for Christ's sake, why don't you go to bed?' and one word led to another, and we got into this violence again, which I deplored.

So I decided to just pack up some clothes and go away from home for a week or so, and by me going away probably, it would bring her back to her senses, and everything would be all right, not knowing that this was what she was hoping I would do, because I was never able to go back home after that.
In other words, this thing backfired on me,

and I guess that's why it hurt me so bad, because I thought that we were able to make up, that she was going to miss me, and was gonna come and get me -- because I went to the YMCA, I didn't even go to a hotel where I could have some other woman or something to come up there and comfort me -- but I went to the YMCA.
So when I got ready to go back home, she had changed all the locks on the door, and that was the thing that started me on my way down.
